extraction.Name: Frances Dubray
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: first mortgaged it for $1600.00, then sold
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: had the patent not been issued there would be no tax
extraction.NOTES: Frances Dubray is deceased (died July 17, 1922 or 1923, deponent unsure). Affidavit given by husband Rufus Eastman, age 40, on May 27, 1929. She received a fee patent for 80 acres; signed receipt before Mr. Covey at Rosebud Agency office. She sold the land for $600.00 in addition to the $1600.00 mortgage, totaling $2200.00 all told. Sale was a cash deal; no fraud alleged. Left five children still living, supported by St. Francis school (board and clothes) and trust funds; when not in school they stay with their grandmother. Deponent states patent should not have been issued as they were making their home on the place at the time; buildings cost him a lot of work and money, and taxes were considerable.
